items.t: Joined a coalition of attorneys general challenging President Trump's declaration of a national emergency and his diversion of funds for border wall construction (2019).
items.q: Attorney General Peter F. Neronha and attorneys general from 20 states today joined in challenging President Trump's declaration of a national emergency and his attempt to divert funding appropriated by Congress for other purposes.

items.t: Submitted four new gun control bills to the General Assembly with Governor Gina Raimondo as part of a package of gun control reforms.
items.q: Governor Gina M. Raimondo and Attorney General Peter Neronha were joined this afternoon by legislative leaders, activists, and members of law enforcement as they unveiled their package of comprehensive gun safety reforms. In addition to four new bills they have submitted to the General Assembly

items.t: Supports legislation to ensure that firearms are safely stored and kept.
items.q: to ensure that firearms are safely stored and kept. The legislation announced today advances all of these goals, and this Office strongly supports all of them.

items.t: Said the state has not invested enough in Medicaid reimbursement rates and that hospitals will remain challenged unless the way healthcare is paid for changes.
items.q: because the state hasn't invested enough in Medicaid reimbursement rates, those hospitals are always going to be challenged unless we change the fundamentals of how we pay for healthcare.

items.t: Said he is concerned about the largely unregulated solar sales industry and the state's lack of strategic thinking on implementing clean energy programs.
items.q: I am also greatly concerned about the largely unregulated solar sales industry, as well as the state’s overall lack of strategic thinking regarding implementation of clean energy programs.

items.t: Said the Division of Public Utilities and carriers need to step up and be skeptical of what big energy is promising.
items.q: I think the Division of Public Utilities and carriers really need to step up in the next administration and have a better sense of what its role is, and frankly be skeptical of what big energy is promising us.

items.t: Announced a new Memorandum of Understanding with the Diocese of Providence as a next step in his Office's review of clergy child sexual abuse.
items.q: Attorney General Peter F. Neronha today announced an important next step in the Office's review of clergy child sexual abuse: a new Memorandum of Understanding between the Attorney General and the Diocese of Providence

items.t: Said his office will be ready if there is any election interference, working with other attorneys general or individually.
items.q: But whether it's working in concert with other attorneys general or working individually here at home, we'll be ready if there is any election interference.

items.t: Said he is frustrated with how state government is operating and that it is not aggressive enough for Rhode Islanders.
items.q: I've gotten… frustrated with how our state government is operating. It's just not aggressive enough for Rhode Islanders, not posing enough leadership.

items.t: Said businesses that deceive consumers for profit should heed the Smart Green lawsuit as a warning.
items.q: Businesses that deceive consumers for profit should heed this lawsuit as a warning; our Consumer Protection Unit continues to grow in size and talent, and we will weed out companies that don’t play by the rules.

record.t: Launched the Attorney General's office cold case unit in 2023.
record.q: Neronha launched his office’s cold case unit in 2023 to solve the multiple cold cases that have plagued the state

record.t: Began an investigation in 2019 into clergy abuse in the Diocese of Providence, in which the Diocese agreed to voluntarily produce internal records dating back to 1950 (2019).
record.q: The investigation began in 2019 when, as a result of a Memorandum of Understanding between the Attorney General and former Bishop Thomas J. Tobin, the Diocese agreed to voluntarily produce internal records relating to clergy abuse dating back to 1950.

record.t: Was elected Rhode Island's 74th Attorney General on November 6, 2018, and sworn in on January 1, 2019.
record.q: On November 6, 2018, Peter F. Neronha was elected as Rhode Island’s 74th Attorney General. He was sworn in on January 1, 2019.

record.office: United States Attorney for the District of Rhode Island
record.t: Served as United States Attorney for the District of Rhode Island from 2009 to 2017.
record.q: At the appointment of President Barack Obama, Mr. Neronha served as the United States Attorney for the District of Rhode Island from 2009 to 2017.

record.t: Joined the United States Attorney’s Office as an Assistant United States Attorney in 2002 and served as Chief of the Organized Crime Strike Force.
record.q: Mr. Neronha went on to join the United States Attorney’s Office as an Assistant United States Attorney in 2002. During his time in that office, Mr. Neronha served in several roles, including as Chief of the Organized Crime Strike Force.

record.office: Rhode Island Special Assistant Attorney General
record.t: Was appointed a Rhode Island Special Assistant Attorney General in 1996 and later an Assistant Attorney General.
record.q: Mr. Neronha’s career in public service began in 1996, when he was appointed as a Rhode Island Special Assistant Attorney General, and later was appointed as an Assistant Attorney General.

record.office: United States Attorney for the District of Rhode Island
record.t: Was appointed to terms on the Attorney General’s Advisory Committee.
record.q: he was appointed by United States Attorney General Eric Holder and later Attorney General Loretta Lynch to terms on the Attorney General’s Advisory Committee.

record.t: Announced a lawsuit against Smart Green Solar, LLC and its CEO Jasjit Gotra under the Rhode Island Deceptive Trade Practice Act.
record.q: Attorney General Peter F. Neronha today announced the filing of a lawsuit against Smart Green Solar, LLC (Smart Green) and its CEO Jasjit Gotra for violating the Rhode Island Deceptive Trade Practice Act (DTPA)

record.t: Announced a motion to amend and supplement the complaint against Smart Green Solar, LLC and its CEO Jasjit Gotra.
record.q: Attorney General Peter F. Neronha today announced the Office has filed a motion to amend and supplement the Office’s complaint against Smart Green Solar, LLC (Smart Green) and its CEO Jasjit Gotra

record.t: Announced the closing of the cases surrounding the deaths of Debra Stone and Cynthia McKenna, who died of asphyxiation.
record.q: Debra Stone and Cynthia McKenna both died of asphyxiation 23 years apart in the Ocean State, Rhode Island Attorney General Peter Neronha announced Wednesday.
